items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A nonfiction book has a photo of a butterfly on a flower. Below the photo, it reads: 'A monarch butterfly feeds on milkweed flowers in a meadow. Monarch butterflies use milkweed as their only food source as caterpillars.'

What text feature is the sentence below the photo, and what information does it give that the photo cannot?

steps: A sentence below a photo is a caption.

The photo shows a butterfly on a flower, but the caption gives: the species (monarch butterfly), the plant (milkweed), the location (a meadow), and the fact that monarch caterpillars eat only milkweed.
solution.answer: This is a caption. It gives the butterfly's name, the plant species, and the fact that monarch caterpillars eat only milkweed — none of which the photo alone can show.

Read the article below.

You are reading a book about sea creatures and come across the word 'bioluminescence.' You want to know what this word means.

Which text feature at the back of a nonfiction book would help you find the definition?

steps: Definitions of important words are found in a glossary.
The index gives page numbers, not definitions.
Use the glossary and look under B for 'bioluminescence.'
solution.answer: Use the glossary. It provides definitions of important vocabulary words. Look under B for 'bioluminescence.'

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A book about geography has sections with these labels in large bold type at the start of each:
- Mountains and Valleys
- Deserts and Grasslands
- Oceans and Coasts

What text feature are these labels?

steps: Labels that appear before sections in a nonfiction text are called subheadings.
They tell the reader what each section is about.
solution.answer: These are subheadings. They tell the reader what topic each section covers.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A science book about the solar system has a diagram of the planets in order from the sun. Each planet is labeled. Below the diagram reads: 'The eight planets in our solar system orbit the sun at different distances and speeds. Mercury, the closest planet, completes a year in just 88 Earth days.'

A student asks: 'I can already see the planet names on the diagram. Why do I need the caption?'

Explain what the caption adds that the diagram labels cannot.

steps: The diagram labels show names and positions of planets.
The caption adds: all planets orbit the sun at different distances and speeds, and Mercury completes a year in 88 Earth days.
Labels identify what something is; captions explain what it does or why it matters.
solution.answer: The diagram labels only show names and positions. The caption explains that planets orbit at different distances and speeds, and gives a specific fact about Mercury's orbit length. Labels name things; captions explain processes and add context.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A student is writing a report about Martin Luther King Jr. She finds a history book. She needs to: (a) find the definition of 'civil disobedience,' and (b) find every page where the Montgomery Bus Boycott is discussed.

Which text feature should she use for each task?

steps: For the definition of 'civil disobedience': use the glossary.
For all pages about the Montgomery Bus Boycott: use the index and look under M.
solution.answer: For the definition of 'civil disobedience,' she should use the glossary. For finding every page that discusses the Montgomery Bus Boycott, she should use the index and look under M.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A book about animal defenses has the word 'camouflage' in bold on page 14. The same word appears again on pages 22 and 31, but is not in bold.

Why do you think the author bolded 'camouflage' on page 14 but not on pages 22 and 31?

steps: Authors typically bold a term the first time it appears — when it is being introduced and defined.
On page 14, camouflage is introduced as a new vocabulary term.
By pages 22 and 31, the reader already knows the word, so bolding it again is unnecessary.
solution.answer: The author bolded 'camouflage' on page 14 because that is when the word is first introduced and defined. By pages 22 and 31, the reader already knows the term, so bold print is no longer needed.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A student is reading a nonfiction book about ancient Rome. The book has: a table of contents, subheadings, bold vocabulary, captions, a glossary, and an index.

The student has these three questions: (1) What chapter covers Roman government? (2) What does 'senate' mean? (3) Are there any photos of the Colosseum, and what do they show?

For each question, name the best text feature to use and explain why.

steps: Question 1: Use the table of contents — it lists chapters and their topics, helping find the chapter about Roman government.
Question 2: Use the glossary — it gives definitions of vocabulary words like 'senate.'
Question 3: Look for photos in the chapter on Roman architecture and read their captions — captions explain what photos show.
solution.answer: 1) Table of contents — to find which chapter covers Roman government. 2) Glossary — to find the definition of 'senate.' 3) Captions under photos in the chapter — to learn what photos of the Colosseum show and their significance.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A nonfiction book about climate change has the following features: bold text for key terms like 'greenhouse gas,' 'carbon footprint,' and 'renewable energy'; subheadings like 'What Causes Climate Change?' and 'How Can We Help?'; and a glossary and index at the back.

A student reads the book straight through from beginning to end without using any text features. Explain two ways that reading without text features makes her experience less effective than it could be.

steps: Without using subheadings: she reads every section even if she only needs information from one part, wasting time.
Without using bold print: she does not know which words are key vocabulary terms and may not focus on learning them.
Without the glossary: when she encounters 'carbon footprint,' she has no easy way to find its definition.
Without the index: after finishing, she cannot quickly return to specific pages about renewable energy.
solution.answer: Two ways reading without text features is less effective: 1) Without subheadings, she reads sections she may not need instead of jumping to relevant parts. 2) Without paying attention to bold print, she misses which words are key vocabulary terms and may not stop to learn them.
